guides.title: Create a New Employee's Account
guides.intro: Create the identity a new employee signs in with, in Meridian Identity, and give it the standard access for the department. Fictional sample written for this portfolio.
guides.prereq:
The onboarding request is checked and assigned to you.
You have the Identity administrator role in Meridian Identity.
You have the HR record open: legal name, start date, manager, department, location and job title.
guides.warn: Enter the attributes exactly as the HR record has them. Payroll, badges and expenses read them from the identity every night.
guides.done: The user's page shows Inactive until the start date, the department and location groups, the Standard employee licence, and a pre-registered device.

steps.title: Select Users, and then select New user
steps.body: The new-user form opens with the fields the HR record fills.

steps.title: Enter the name, the start date, and the department
steps.body: The account stays inactive until 08:00 on the start date. Let the system propose the account name: the mailbox and home drive use it.

steps.title: Check the groups and the licence
steps.body: The department and location groups come from the request. The Standard employee licence creates the mailbox within an hour.

steps.title: Select Create
steps.body: If the page shows Attribute conflict, another account has the same employee number. Don't create a second identity: send the request back to HR.

steps.title: Pre-register the laptop, and then generate the enrolment link
steps.body: Enter the serial number from the hardware order. Copy the enrolment link into the request's welcome message; it works for fourteen days from the start date.

guides.title: Unlock a Customer's Account
guides.intro: Internal procedure for support agents of Ledgerly: a customer is locked out and can't wait for the lock to lift. Verify who you're talking to before you change anything. Fictional sample written for this portfolio.
guides.prereq:
The customer has opened a ticket and is in the conversation with you.
You have the Support agent role in the support console.
guides.warn: Never unlock on the request of someone who isn't the account holder or an administrator of the company, however urgent the request sounds.
guides.done: The Sign-in tab shows Unlocked by with your name and the ticket number, the customer can sign in, and the ticket note says what you did and why.

steps.title: Find the account by its email address
steps.body: The customer record opens with the ticket beside it.

steps.title: Check that the customer is verified in this conversation
steps.body: The green banner names the method and the time. Without it, send a verification code first.

steps.title: Review the recent sign-in attempts
steps.body: Attempts from the customer's usual location and device point to a mistyped password. Attempts from elsewhere mean you reset the password instead of unlocking.

steps.title: Select Unlock, or send a reset link if the customer isn't sure of the password
steps.body: Enter the ticket number as the reason. A reset link unlocks the account when it's used.

steps.title: Check the confirmation, and then record what you did in the ticket
steps.body: The customer receives an email that support unlocked the account.

guides.title: Add an Environment Variable to a Relay and Deploy It
guides.intro: Give the relay the token your application expects, from the Lattice Cloud console, and deploy the change. Fictional sample written for this portfolio: the console and the service are invented.
guides.prereq:
You have the Developer role in the project.
You have the token your application expects in the Authorization header.
guides.warn: A value is stored encrypted and never shown again after you save it. Keep it in your password manager as well.
guides.done: The deployment shows Live with a passing health check, and the variable's row shows today's date under Last set.

steps.title: Open the relay, and then select the Configuration tab
steps.body: The tab lists every environment variable with the date it was last set. Values other than the target URL are never shown.

steps.title: Check the target URL
steps.body: Select Edit if your application's address has changed. The relay posts every delivery to it.

steps.title: Select Add on the empty row, and then enter the name and the value
steps.body: Choose the environments the value applies to. Reference it in relay.yaml as ${RELAY_TARGET_TOKEN}.

steps.title: Select Deploy changes
steps.body: A changed variable takes effect at the next deployment, not before.

steps.title: Check that the deployment is live and the health check passed
steps.body: The new deployment is at the top of the list. A failed health check keeps the previous deployment serving traffic.

guides.title: Record the Readings for a Monthly Pump Inspection
guides.intro: Record the four inspection readings for a feed pump in the maintenance console, then close the work order. Fictional sample written for this portfolio: it isn't an operating instruction for real equipment.
guides.prereq:
You're signed in to the maintenance console as a technician on the shift the work order is assigned to.
You have the readings from the local gauges.
guides.warn: Stay outside the guard while the pump runs. Take every reading from a gauge or the console.
guides.done: The work order shows Ready to close, and all four results are inside their expected range.

steps.title: Open the work order and select Record readings
steps.body: The work order lists the four checks and their expected values.

steps.title: Enter each reading as shown on the local gauge, then select Save readings
steps.body: Enter the discharge pressure in bar, the bearing temperature in °C, the vibration in mm/s, and whether the seal leaks.

steps.title: Check that all four results are inside their range, then select Close work order
steps.body: If a result is outside its range, don't close the work order. Report the reading to your supervisor.

guides.title: Schedule a Report for Automatic Delivery
guides.intro: Send a report to the people who need it every week or every month, without opening Beacon Reports on the day. Fictional sample written for this portfolio: the application is invented.
guides.prereq:
You can open the report you want to send.
You have the recipients' email addresses.
guides.done: A message confirms the schedule and names the next delivery, and the report's Schedules tab lists it.

steps.title: Open the report, and then select Schedule
steps.body: The schedule dialog opens.

steps.title: Enter each recipient and press Enter
steps.body: Each address appears as a chip under the field. Recipients don't need a Beacon account.

steps.title: Choose how often, the day, and the time
steps.body: The time is shown in your time zone. The report uses the data available at that moment.

steps.title: Choose the format, and then select Preview
steps.body: PDF for a report people read, Spreadsheet for one they work with. The preview shows the subject, the attachment's name and the recipients.

steps.title: Select Save schedule
steps.body: The dialog closes and a message names the next delivery.

steps.title: Check the schedule on the Schedules tab
steps.body: Select Edit to change it or Pause to stop it without deleting it.
